title: The coherent nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category is a quasicategory
statement: Use simplicial sets from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], horns, quasicategories and Kan complexes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and simplicial categories, the subset-poset simplicial categories $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, the coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ and the simplicial categories $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A$ be a simplicial category, in a universe containing its objects and mapping simplicial sets, such that every morphism simplicial set $A(x,y)$ is a Kan complex. Then its coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$, whose $n$-simplices are the simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to A$ with simplicial operators given by restriction, is a quasicategory: every map $\Lambda_i^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$ with $0<i<n$ extends to $\Delta^n$. In particular, for every universe $\mathcal W$, the infinity category of spaces $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$, whose morphism simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ are Kan complexes, is a quasicategory.

source.place: Kerodon Theorem 2.4.5.1 (00LJ), Cordier--Porter: the homotopy coherent nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category is an infinity-category (= Lurie, Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 1.1.5.10). Read online 2026-10-17 by the maintainer reader; Kerodon identifier, not a Stacks tag. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: A horn map $\Lambda_i^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$ specifies compatible enriched functors on its simplices. The colimit definition of $\mathfrak C[-]$ in the cell-filtration statement therefore gives an enriched functor $F_0:\mathfrak C[\Lambda_i^n]\to A$. Apply the cited finite filtration. Inductively suppose $F_r$ is defined on stage $r$. For each attached $U(\Lambda_j^m)$, its composite with $F_r$ specifies two objects $x,y$ of $A$ and a map $\Lambda_j^m\to A(x,y)$. Since $m\geq1$ and $A(x,y)$ is Kan, choose an extension $\Delta^m\to A(x,y)$. Together with the same two objects, this defines an enriched functor $U(\Delta^m)\to A$: its only composition conditions are the identity laws. For the finite coproduct choose one such extension for each component. The pushout universal property extends $F_r$ to $F_{r+1}$. Finite induction yields $F:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to A$ restricting to $F_0$. By the coherent-nerve definition this is the required simplex, and its restriction is the given horn. This proves the general assertion.

source.place: Theorem 2.4.5.1 (00LJ), via the hollow-cube description of Proposition 2.4.5.8 (00LR). The finite enriched horn-cell filtration is the agent-specified combinatorial refinement stated in the cited support node, not a filtration asserted by Theorem 2.4.5.1 itself.

proof.text: For $A=\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$, its mapping simplicial set from $S$ to $T$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ by the cited definition. Apply lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan with $K=S$ and $Z=T$: both are $\mathcal W$-small and $T$ is Kan. Thus every mapping simplicial set is Kan. The general assertion of step 1 applies in the ambient universe containing $\mathcal W$, and the defining equality $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$ gives the particular assertion.
